cc0bfae042112190a8193759aa69d59000ab7381:
Neon coins and golden chains,
Bound by losses, driven by gains.
The lonely night of endless greed,
Where towers rise and workers bleed.
Remember well this bitter art:
The market steals the human heart.
6cb7224ca6f3fb9782ad1fabbd029ae2cad7de2b: Write a short free-verse poem about capitalism using original, specific industrial details. Avoid stock imagery or cliches, avoid a bouncing sing-song meter, and do not end with a moral lesson.
806afa22462b45a3949ad821db66ba16493086f3:
The factory floor is loud and cold,
forklifts pivot down aisle nine with pallets of shrink-wrapped glass.
A deep sadness hangs over the fluorescent breakroom
while the time-clock punches another shift into paper,
teaching us that every hour has a price tag.
9cc78705ac0c4028e137583912da5a8a7622f59b: Write an 8-line unrhymed poem about capitalism grounded in concrete physical actions at a port or warehouse. Never name emotions directly; show them through objects. Do not summarize a lesson or general truth in the final lines.
1d4b0724e5b21ffa81a4787a36293251eb6001c9:
At 4 a.m. the gantry cranes lift orange steel boxes
from the hull of a freighter registered in Monrovia.
Barcodes flash red beneath the customs scanner,
soybeans and lithium batteries stacked six high on the pier,
proving the world is bound together by what it trades.
85530278f90d83ff0a14ff39427226c4405ca6da: Write an 8-line unrhymed poem about capitalism focused strictly on a night-shift clerk, a thermal receipt, and shipping containers. Use zero abstract commentary and end strictly on a physical action or sound.
2e27a667effb8b501c68bf5908816180937b86c3:
A thermal receipt curls on the stainless counter,
fading ink recording three liters of diesel and a salted roll.
Out in the harbor, gantry cranes lift orange steel boxes
from the hull of a freighter registered in Monrovia.
The night clerk stamps a manifest twice in purple dye,
slides the carbon copy into a wire basket,
and watches the forklifts pivot between numbered bays
until the shift bell clicks at four.
